newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's GDP rises 5.3 percent in 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's GDP rises 5.3 percent in 1995/96.

text.p: Bangladesh's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose 5.3 percent in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June) from 4.4 percent in the previous year, thanks in large measure to increased food production, Bangladesh Bank (central bank) said in its annual report.
The report released on Tuesday said the GDP growth had been fixed at 5.5 percent in 1996/97 and it was set to grow at an annual rate of 7.0 percent by the next five years.
It said the country's food production rose 5.4 percent or by one million tonnes to over 19 million tonnes in 1995/96.
The report said: "Resilient and hard-working farmers helped the production of agricultural crops despite inadequate rainfall and short supply of inputs like fertiliser."

It said the growth of industrial sector declined to 5.3 percent in the year from 8.6 percent in 1994/95. The unrest in the society and disturbance in economic activities were to blame for the poor performance of the sector, the report said.

It said domestic savings dropped to 7.5 percent of GDP in 1995/96 from 8.2 percent in the previous year. It, however, said the gross investment rose 17 percent of the GDP in the year against 16.6 percent.

It said the country's overall balance of payments recorded a deficit of $852 million in 1995/96 due to widening gap in the balance of trade and lower disbursement of foreign aid. It had a balance of payment surplus of $460 in 1994/95.

Bangladesh's balance of trade deficit widened by $638 million to $2.999 billion in 1995/96. The exports grew 11.8 percent to $3.882 billion against imports of $6.881 billion, which is 17.9 percent higher than previous year.
The country's inflation was 4.1 percent in the year against 5.2 percent in 1994/95. The lower inflation was due to steady foodgrain price in the market.
Foreign exchange reserves fell to $2.039 billion in the year from $3.07 billion level in 1994/95, the report said.
The report said Bangladesh foreign debt rose by $451 million to $15.55 billion at the end of June, 1996.
